_note: How each core lays out real-time-clock state. Unlike the other files here this one is NOT
synced from the registry pages: the specifications do not describe clock layouts. These come
from files real cores wrote, or the core's own source where no file has been sampled, cross-checked
against one-saves-convert's rtc module. A core absent from this file records no clock convention,
which is also what a core gets whose source is unpublished and whose files nobody has sampled.
A core's entry is the core as its kind hosts it. A libretro frontend writes a libretro core's save
memory to <name>.srm and the clock it exposes to <name>.rtc, so every libretro core here is a sidecar,
whatever its standalone build does. An app that ships a build of its own and lays the clock out
differently is listed under the core's `apps`, keyed by app slug.
Layouts: appended | packed | sidecar. A footer (appended or packed) states timestamp_width, the
bytes its host clock takes. A sidecar states its `record`: origin (timestamp_width, byte_order),
registers (timestamp_width), sameboy, or packed-seiko. Which chip the state belongs to is the save's
own business: mostly the system, but the MiSTer Game Boy cores also keep a HuC-3 in the same footer,
packed differently, so for those it is the cartridge type. A chip a sidecar's record cannot hold is
one the core keeps no clock for.
Each entry's `evidence` says where its facts were read: a file, or the source at a commit.
